text:
ConocoPhillips fell 0.6% today to $136.27, extending a steep two-week decline of nearly 10% that accelerated sharply after the company reported quarterly earnings on November 5th. The stock has lost roughly $18 per share since late October, suggesting investors reacted negatively to the earnings results or guidance, though the data doesn't spell out what specifically disappointed the market.

The broader backdrop adds pressure: U.S. oil prices have drifted down to $99.64 a barrel (roughly 13% below their late-October levels), and the Democrats' midterm election sweep signals a policy environment more hostile to fossil fuels and more supportive of renewables. While Middle East tensions with Iran remain a potential upside factor for oil prices, the combination of weaker crude, an earnings miss, and an unfavorable political shift appears to have outweighed that risk in investors' calculus.
